title: Narrative Sequencers: after, before, when, by the time
grammarTitle: Narrative Sequencers — Connecting Events in a Story
grammarNote: Sequencers (соединители последовательности) помогают структурировать повествование и показывать порядок событий. В рассказе о прошлом они определяют, какое время глагола использовать: Past Simple или Past Perfect. Важно знать, какой sequencer сочетается с каким временем.

grammarTable.subject: WHEN
grammarTable.example: "When she arrived, he left." (sim) / "When she arrived, he had left." (he left first)

grammarTable.subject: BEFORE
grammarTable.example: "Before she arrived, I had finished." (finish = earlier) / "Before leaving, she called me."

grammarTable.subject: AFTER
grammarTable.example: "After he had finished, he left." (finish = earlier) / "After finishing, he left."

grammarTable.subject: BY THE TIME
grammarTable.example: "By the time he arrived, she had already left." (arrive = later → leave = PP)

grammarTable.subject: ONCE
grammarTable.example: "Once I had finished, I felt relieved." (once = when completed — triggers PP for the earlier action)

grammarTable.subject: AS SOON AS
grammarTable.example: "As soon as she arrived, she called me." / "As soon as he had spoken, he regretted it."

rows.example: "When she walked in, everyone stopped talking." (same moment → both PS)
"When I arrived, she HAD ALREADY LEFT." (she left before I arrived → PP)
"When Amir looked back, he realised he had made the right decision." (realise = PS, made = earlier = PP)

rows.form: WHEN at the start vs end of sentence
rows.example: "When the bus left, I was still there." / "I was still there when the bus left." (same meaning, word order differs)
"Before she arrived (PS), I had finished (PP)." — 'before' introduces the LATER event.
"After he had finished (PP), he left (PS)." — 'after' introduces the EARLIER event.
"After finishing the report, she sent it." / "Before leaving, he said goodbye." (no subject → gerund)
"She had packed her bags before leaving." / "After arriving, she unpacked." ✅

rows.form: Structure: by the time + PS → PP
rows.example: "By the time she ARRIVED (PS), he had GONE (PP)." — by = deadline; earlier action = PP.
"He had gone by the time she arrived." ✅ Same meaning, different word order.
"By the time I reached the hospital, the operation had already started." ✅
"By the time you read this, I will have left." (future perfect — note: different tense)
"Once she had finished crying, she felt better." (finish = earlier; feel better = result)
"Once he arrived, we started the meeting." (simple sequence — no PP needed)

rows.form: AS SOON AS = immediate next action
rows.example: "As soon as the alarm rang, she got up." ✅ (immediate → both PS)

rows.form: AS SOON AS + PP for emphasis
rows.example: "As soon as he had sat down, she started talking." (sat down = earlier by a moment → PP for emphasis)

grammarTip:
Narrative sequencers + past tenses:

WHEN:
- одновременно → оба Past Simple
- одно раньше другого → раннее = PP

BEFORE = позже / AFTER = раньше:
"Before she arrived, I had finished." ✅ (finish = раньше)
"After he had finished, he left." ✅ (finish = раньше)

BY THE TIME:
"By the time + PS → PP"
"By the time I arrived, she had already left." ✅

ONCE + завершение → результат:
"Once I had finished, I felt better." ✅

💡 Правило: КОГДА одно событие явно РАНЬШЕ другого
→ раннее событие = PAST PERFECT
Простая цепочка событий без акцента на порядок
→ можно Past Simple

exercises.hint: "When + PS" followed by earlier action → PP. "When she arrived, he HAD ALREADY LEFT." ✅

exercises.text: "Before the exam started, she ___ (review) all her notes."
exercises.hint: "Before" introduces the LATER event → earlier action = PP. "Before the exam started (PS), she HAD REVIEWED (PP)." ✅

exercises.text: "By the time Amir ___ (arrive) at the exam, everything ___ (go) wrong."
exercises.hint: "By the time + PS" → earlier event = PP. "By the time Amir ARRIVED, everything HAD GONE wrong." ✅

exercises.text: "After he ___ (finish) the presentation, he felt relieved."
exercises.hint: "After" introduces the EARLIER event → PP. "After he HAD FINISHED (PP), he felt relieved (PS)." ✅

exercises.text: "___ leaving, he said goodbye." Is this correct?
opts: Yes — "before + gerund" when there's no subject
Yes but only in informal speech
exercises.correct: Yes — "before + gerund" when there's no subject
exercises.hint: "Before LEAVING, he said goodbye." ✅ When there's no separate subject, use gerund after before/after.

exercises.text: "___ I arrived at the party, most of the food had been eaten."
exercises.hint: "BY THE TIME I arrived + PP" — most food eaten BEFORE my arrival. "By the time I ARRIVED, most food HAD BEEN EATEN." ✅

exercises.text: "She finished her essay, then submitted it, then went to sleep." — Should Past Perfect be used?
opts: Yes — always use PP for sequences
No — simple sequence in story = Past Simple is fine
PP for all except "went to sleep"
exercises.correct: No — simple sequence in story = Past Simple is fine
exercises.hint: Simple sequential story with "then" = Past Simple. PP is for when you specifically signal that one action is BEFORE another reference point. ✅

exercises.text: "Once she ___ (receive) the results, she called her parents."
exercises.hint: "Once" can use PS (simple sequence) or PP (completion emphasis). "Once she RECEIVED/HAD RECEIVED..." — both ✅.

exercises.text: "As soon as he ___ home, he ___ a shower."
exercises.hint: "As soon as" = immediate sequence → both Past Simple. "As soon as he GOT home, he TOOK a shower." ✅ (both actions in quick sequence)

exercises.instruction: Complete with the correct verb form.
exercises.text: "When Rustam walked into the office, the professor ___ (already / leave)."
exercises.hint: "When + PS" followed by earlier action → PP. "HAD ALREADY LEFT." ✅

exercises.text: "She had already finished by the time I arrived." — Is this correct?
opts: No — "by the time" must come first
Yes — "by the time" can come at the end
Yes, but only in informal English
exercises.correct: Yes — "by the time" can come at the end
exercises.hint: "She HAD ALREADY FINISHED by the time I arrived." ✅ "By the time" can go at either end of the sentence.

exercises.text: Choose the sentence that correctly shows sequence.
exercises.hint: "Before + PS" → earlier action = PP. "Before she ARRIVED (PS), I HAD FINISHED (PP)." ✅

questions.text: "By the time she arrived, he ___ left." Choose.
questions.hint: "By the time + PS → HAD + PP." "By the time she arrived, he HAD left." ✅

questions.text: "Before the exam started, she ___ all her notes." Choose.
questions.hint: "Before + PS" → earlier action = PP. "She HAD REVIEWED all her notes before the exam started." ✅
"After" introduces EARLIER action → PP. "After he HAD FINISHED, he went home." ✅

questions.text: "When she walked in, everyone ___ (stop) talking." — simultaneous
questions.hint: Simultaneous/immediate → Past Simple. "When she walked in, everyone STOPPED." ✅ No PP needed for simultaneous.

questions.text: "___ the lecture started, she had already taken her seat."
questions.hint: "BY THE TIME + PS → PP." "By the time the lecture started, she had already taken her seat." ✅

questions.text: "Before leaving, she said goodbye." — "leaving" here is:
questions.hint: "Before LEAVING" = before + gerund. When there's no separate subject, use the -ing form after before/after. ✅

questions.text: "Once she ___ finished, she felt better." Choose.
questions.hint: "Once she HAD FINISHED" = once + PP, expressing completion. Then result follows. ✅

questions.text: "As soon as he arrived, she ___." Best choice:
questions.hint: "As soon as" = immediate sequence → both PS. "As soon as he arrived, she LEFT." ✅

questions.text: "Before" introduces the ___ event in the sequence.
questions.hint: "BEFORE" + the LATER event → the earlier event uses PP. "Before she arrived (later), I had finished (earlier PP)." ✅

questions.text: "After" introduces the ___ event in the sequence.
questions.hint: "AFTER" + EARLIER event (PP) → result/later action (PS). "After he had finished (earlier), he left (later)." ✅

questions.text: "She finished her project, said goodbye, and left." — These use ___ tense.
questions.hint: Simple narrative sequence → Past Simple. No PP needed when "then" or simple sequence is clear. ✅

questions.text: "By the time the professor arrived, Rustam ___ waiting for an hour."
questions.hint: "By the time + PS → Past Perfect." "Rustam HAD BEEN waiting for an hour." (Perfect Continuous for duration before another past) ✅

opts: "When she had arrived, he had left."
All three are possible but with different meanings
questions.correct: All three are possible but with different meanings
questions.hint: All three CAN work: (1) he left AS she arrived; (2) he left BEFORE she arrived; (3) both actions both earlier (rare). Context determines which. ✅

questions.text: "Once I had arrived, I felt better." — "had arrived" here is:
opts: Past Perfect showing the arrival was complete before feeling better
questions.correct: Past Perfect showing the arrival was complete before feeling better
questions.hint: "Once I had ARRIVED (PP completion) → I felt better (result)." ✅ PP after "once" is natural for showing completion.

questions.text: "___ the bus left, she was still running towards the stop."
questions.hint: "BY THE TIME / WHEN the bus left, she was still running." Both work — "by the time" implies a deadline missed. ✅

questions.text: "After finishing the report, she submitted it." Can we expand this to use a subject and Past Perfect?
opts: Yes: "After she had finished the report, she submitted it."
No — must use Past Simple both times
Yes but only in formal writing
questions.correct: Yes: "After she had finished the report, she submitted it."
questions.hint: "After she HAD FINISHED (PP) → she submitted (PS)." ✅ Gerund form and full clause with PP both work with "after."
